title: An over-long line still reaches QuickBooks Online and matches the report
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin (all permissions) at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) on the What/Why QuickBooks host (for example qb1.qa.shopview.com).
  • The shop has an active QuickBooks Online connection to sandbox company {Sandbox-company-A} (for example ShopView QA Sandbox), and you can sign in to that sandbox.
  • Require Tech Story (Settings, Work Orders tab) is off.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-A09 Fleet) has a contact person and an asset, {Asset-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-A09 Truck).
  • Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) is open for {Customer-A} and {Asset-A} at {Location-A}, not invoiced.
  • {Work-order-1} has a labor line {Line-1} whose Title is exactly 16 characters (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-A9) and whose Description is the letter é repeated 3,000 times, with no tech story.
  • {Work-order-1} was completed and invoiced while the connection was active, as invoice {Invoice-A} (for example 10234), dated {Invoice-date-A} (for example 13 Oct 2026).
custom_steps:
1. Sign in to QuickBooks Online and open sandbox company {Sandbox-company-A}.
  2. Open the invoice for {Customer-A} that matches {Invoice-A}.
  3. Copy {Line-1}'s Description into a Google Sheets cell and count it with =LEN.
  4. In ShopView, open the QuickBooks Unexported Items list.
  5. Look for {Invoice-A} in the list.
  6. In ShopView, open the Reports page and click Export Reports (if it is not there, open it from Administration).
  7. Choose the Customer Invoice report.
  8. Set the date range to cover {Invoice-date-A}.
  9. Download the report.
  10. Open the downloaded file in a spreadsheet (for example Google Sheets: File, Import, Upload).
  11. Find the row for {Line-1} on invoice {Invoice-A} and read its ItemDescription cell.
  12. Compare the Description from step 3 with the ItemDescription from step 11, character by character.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: the invoice is in QuickBooks Online: the over-long line did not stop it from syncing.
  • Step 3: the count is 2,009 (16 + 3 + 1,990 letters é, the most that fit in 4,000), the text starts with the full title and " - ", and the last letter is a whole é.
  • Step 5: {Invoice-A} is not in the Unexported Items list.
  • Step 12: the two texts are identical: both routes are cut at the same place.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11257; story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks); PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It (What/Why)", Confluence 845348896, version of 13 Oct 2026, S3-E3, S3-R7, S3-R4, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 2.2 (The long end), 13 Oct copy; tech plan "Title and Description - Technical Implementation Plan" (dated 2026-09-23, shared by the QA lead 13 Oct 2026), FR-011; Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (a What/Why QA build exists; verification by the build verification session).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-E3: “A description long enough to be cut still syncs. The invoice reaches QuickBooks; it does not land in Unexported Items.”
  • S3-R7: “When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.”
  • S3-R4: “The same text is used by the live QuickBooks sync and by the downloadable Customer Invoice report. The two can never show different text for the same line.”
  • SV-10132 acceptance criteria: “Given a joined text longer than the QuickBooks limit, when it is sent, then it is shortened from the end, the cut does not fall inside a character, the title is intact, and the invoice syncs rather than landing in Unexported Items.”
